subject: Follow-up on your managed instances showing as disconnected
body:
Hi Wendell,

Thank you for your time during the call.

The line was noisy in places, so this lists only what I am sure about and what we still need to confirm.

What we understood:
- Two of your five managed Core instances show as disconnected since the Central Management upgrade.
- A red label appears next to them.

Still to confirm:
- The version: both 7.5.2 and 7.4.2 were mentioned.
- The upgrade day.
- Whether you restarted the service or rebooted the server.
- The exact text of the red label.

Next steps:
1. You: send a screenshot of the red label and the Central Management log from the upgrade day.
2. You: confirm the version from the About page, the upgrade day and what you restarted.
3. Me: review the documentation on reconnecting instances after an upgrade, then follow up in writing.

Background: https://docs.example-opswat.invalid/central-management/instances/managing-connected-instances

claims_needing_verification.claim: The installed Central Management version is 7.5.2.
claims_needing_verification.reason: The customer first said 7.5.2 and later said it might be 7.4.2; the first mention was also low-confidence audio.

claims_needing_verification.claim: The upgrade was done on Sunday.
claims_needing_verification.reason: The customer later said it may have been Saturday and will check their change record.

claims_needing_verification.claim: The customer restarted only the Central Management service and did not reboot the server.
claims_needing_verification.reason: The account changed between a service restart, a full server reboot and a reboot of a Core machine.

claims_needing_verification.claim: The red label says authentication failed or token expired.
claims_needing_verification.reason: The customer could not read the label exactly and the transcript segment has very low confidence.
